 Spokesperson Ham In-kyung: "What Has the Government Been Doing but Watching?"
 Politics | Published 2026.11.07. 14:56:52 | By Lee Seung-ryung yigija94@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A A view of Kukkiwon in Seoul's Gangnam district on Friday, as concerns mount over the impact on South Korea's standing as taekwondo's birthplace after the martial art's listing on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a "traditional North Korean martial art" became all but certain. Yonhap News The People Power Party on the 7th criticized the government over the near-certain listing of taekwondo, South Korea's national martial art, on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a "traditional North Korean martial art," saying, "What has the government been doing but watching?"
 Ham In-kyung, spokesperson for the People Power Party, said in a commentary that day, "Must we even defer to North Korea when it comes to protecting the Republic of Korea's cultural heritage?"
 Ham said, "What is even more appalling is the Korea Heritage Service's response," pointing out that "ahead of the announcement of the review results, a private organization asked the agency to deliver an official letter to UNESCO explaining the case for a joint inter-Korean listing of taekwondo, but while the Korea Heritage Service responded that it had sent the letter, the organization claims it was never actually delivered."
 Ham added, "If true, this goes beyond mere administrative negligence and amounts to deceiving the public," demanding that "the Korea Heritage Service must clearly disclose whether the letter was sent and the circumstances surrounding it."
 Ham stressed, "The government must clearly explain to the international community the Republic of Korea's position on the history and legitimacy of taekwondo," adding, "A government that failed even to protect the Republic of Korea's national martial art must be held accountable before the people for its irresponsibility and incompetence."
